content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`, with one lodash call moved to `es-toolkit/compat` because the main entry point has no `isEmpty`. I didn't follow the skill's advice, because it is wrong in two places. It says every lodash function exists in `es-toolkit` and that compat should never be used.

- **`tokens`:** it uses `words` from `es-toolkit`. It matched compat's output on every case I tried, including `"Id_MAX "`, `""`, `"fooBar2baz"`, `"ABCdef"`, `"a1b"` and `"12ab"`.
- **`byAge`:** it uses `groupBy(rows, r => r.age)` from `es-toolkit`. The string shorthand `'age'` isn't accepted by the main entry point, so I used a small arrow function. Keys come out as strings, as before.
- **`isBlank`:** it uses `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main entry point exports only `isEmptyObject`, and that doesn't match lodash for numbers, booleans, strings or arrays. Compat's `isEmpty` returns `true` for `null`, booleans and numbers, and gives the right answers for strings, arrays and objects. A deeper import path (`es-toolkit/compat/predicate/isEmpty`) isn't exposed by the package, so I used the `es-toolkit/compat` import.

I didn't check `byAge` or `isBlank` against real lodash, because lodash isn't installed. `isBlank` was only checked against compat's own results.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 701 bytes (min+gzip), with 87 bytes of own code. `tsc` reports no errors for `out/module.ts`. The only errors are in `src/module.ts`, where `lodash/*` can't be resolved. The final spot-check script had a quoting error and never ran, so the results above come from the earlier per-function checks.
